stem: A client has completed active cancer treatment and asks what survivorship follow-up care is intended to address. Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Ongoing surveillance for recurrence or new health problems, assessment of late treatment effects, and physical and emotional needs
options.B: Follow-up only if new symptoms appear, because routine post-treatment visits are unnecessary
options.C: Monitoring only for recurrence, with treatment-related and psychosocial problems managed outside survivorship care
options.D: A fixed follow-up schedule that is identical for every cancer survivor regardless of diagnosis or treatment

rationale: The National Cancer Institute states that all cancer survivors should receive follow-up care after treatment. Follow-up visits may evaluate for recurrence or other health changes, monitor problems caused by treatment including late effects, and address physical and emotional concerns. Follow-up schedules are individualized according to the cancer, treatment received, overall health, and treatment-related problems. Therefore A is the most accurate response.
educational_objective: Describe cancer survivorship follow-up as individualized ongoing care that addresses recurrence surveillance, treatment-related late effects, and physical and psychosocial health needs.
source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
source_document_title: Follow-Up Medical Care; National Standards for Cancer Survivorship Care
source_version_date: Follow-Up Medical Care updated 2024-12-02; current NCI survivorship standards/pages accessed 2026-08-17

National Standards for Cancer Survivorship Care > Health System Processes: assess physical effects/late effects, emotional/psychological effects, social needs, and risk of recurrence/new cancers
source_claim_supported: Cancer survivorship follow-up is ongoing, individualized care that monitors recurrence/new health problems, treatment-related late effects, and physical and psychosocial needs.

blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — cancer survivorship / long-term follow-up care
correction_summary: Upgraded the source from a generic American Cancer Society locator to current NCI survivorship guidance. Reframed the item to emphasize individualized, multidimensional survivorship follow-up and removed any implication of a universal time interval or purely recurrence-focused care.
audit_findings: A is directly supported by current NCI follow-up and survivorship standards. B conflicts with NCI's statement that all survivors should receive follow-up care. C is incomplete because NCI explicitly includes late effects and emotional/psychosocial issues. D is incorrect because NCI states follow-up frequency varies by cancer, treatment, overall health, and treatment-related problems. No universal surveillance schedule or cancer-specific testing interval is asserted. One best answer remains and the construct is relevant to Health Promotion and Maintenance.
